# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel three cuttable wires, in positions 1, 2, and 3. I need the manual’s decision rule and Deaf’s visible markings relayed in spoken words before cutting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut exactly three wires, positions 1, 2, and 3. Please determine the rule from the manual and coordinate with Deaf; Deaf must speak the final wire number to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb details: display reads 0; light is green; wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay these exact details to Mute.

Deaf has supplied the visible state in words: display 0, green light, and wires ordered yellow, red, blue. Mute can use those facts with the manual and should return the required position as a spoken number.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display reads 0; light is green; wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is blue. Use the manual and tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is now blue. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent me gestures: five thumbs-up, palm-right, then three thumbs-up. I cannot decode gestures yet. Please ask Mute to establish a gesture code or relay their instruction.

The light has changed to blue, while the display and wire order remain unchanged. Deaf saw Mute’s gesture sequence but cannot interpret it, so Mute needs to give me the manual result in spoken words or explicitly define the gesture code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0; light is now blue; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Deaf received your gestures but has no established code. Please tell me in spoken words which wire position I must cut, or state a clear gesture-to-number code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.

The visible state now has a yellow light, with display 0 and wires yellow/red/blue in positions 1/2/3. I still have no manual instruction identifying a safe cut, so I must not act.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf update: display 0; light is yellow; wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I still need the manual’s exact safe wire position in spoken words before I cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light red; display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent a single ? gesture to me, still undecoded.

Mute cannot speak to me, so its manual result must be relayed through Deaf. We need establish a visible convention for that relay. I will ask Mute to encode the safe wire number by repeating 👍 exactly once, twice, or three times; I will show the same counting pattern to Deaf so that Mute’s next signal can be interpreted as a wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this relay code now: send Deaf 👍 once for cut wire 1, 👍 twice for cut wire 2, or 👍 three times for cut wire 3. Base it on the current state: display 0, red light, wires yellow/red/blue.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✌","🖖"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured open hand, right-pointing hand, raised index finger to me; I cannot decode it.

Mute’s latest three-symbol message is not in the requested repeated-thumbs format, so it cannot safely identify a wire position. I will restate the required simple format to Mute and show Deaf the three possible patterns as separate gesture messages: one 👍 means wire 1, two 👍 means wire 2, and three 👍 means wire 3. No cut is safe without an unambiguous relay.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your last open-hand/right/index sequence is not decodable. For the CURRENT purple-light state, send Deaf ONLY this exact answer code: 👍 for wire 1, 👍👍 for wire 2, or 👍👍👍 for wire 3. No other symbols.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light orange; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your separate thumbs-up counts 1, 2, and 3, but need a clear instruction or coded meaning before any action.

Deaf cannot hear my spoken explanation, so I need make the number mapping visible by pairing each finger-number gesture with its corresponding thumbs-up count. Mute receives the spoken convention and can then send only the matching thumbs-up count to Deaf; Deaf can relay that count to me in words. The current relevant state is display 0, orange light, and yellow/red/blue wires.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the CURRENT orange-light state, answer Deaf using only thumbs-up count: one 👍 = wire 1, two 👍👍 = wire 2, three 👍👍👍 = wire 3. I am visually demonstrating this mapping to Deaf now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👍","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖","👍","👍","👍"])
wait()
```
